correctness.rationale: Expand the ideal projector as 2^(-n) times the graph-stabilizer sum. For subset sizes i,j in the two parts, all vertices of part A are supported when j is odd, otherwise just the selected i; likewise B is wholly supported when i is odd, otherwise just the selected j. X and Z at the same vertex still give a nonidentity Pauli. Trace orthogonality and depolarizing eigenvalue r=1-q give a fidelity sum of r^weight, yielding the displayed four terms by splitting (i,j) by parity. Independently for n=4 the weight polynomials are 1+6r^2+9r^4 and 1+2r^2+8r^3+5r^4, recovering the exact 49/256 versus 45/256 at r=1/2. With x=u/t and y=r/t we have x+y=1 and both strictly between zero and one. For b>=a+2, m=b-a-1, subtraction after normalization by t^n/4 gives two positive differences y x^a(1-x^m), x y^a(1-y^m), minus (y-x)(xy)^a(y^m-x^m). If y>x the latter is strictly less than the first positive term, since (y-x)/y, y^a and (y^m-x^m)/(1-x^m) are each in (0,1); if x>y exchange x and y; equality x=y makes the correction zero. Thus all adjacent comparisons are strict, including the last allowed step for either parity of n. The normalized balanced limit is 1 since both sizes diverge; for fixed a only 1+x^a+y^a survives, equal to 2 at a=1. The formula gives 1 and 2^(-n) at the endpoints, where no strict comparison holds. These are exact overlap statements for IID post-preparation depolarization, not entanglement or circuit-preparation thresholds. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and verify.py; the reported VERIFY_OK 3612 is a finite replay, not an all-size certificate. It was not rerun.
